description:
A deep psychological analysis of Lisa Jewell's bestselling thriller Then She Was Gone.

Ten years after fifteen-year-old Ellie Mack vanishes without a trace on her way to the library, her grieving mother Laurel meets charismatic mathematician Floyd Dunn—only to discover his nine-year-old daughter Poppy bears an impossible resemblance to Ellie.

In this comprehensive breakdown, we examine:
- The anatomy of sudden domestic vanishing and lingering guilt
- Maternal projection, ambiguous loss, and emotional arrest
- The terrifying psychology behind Noelle Donnelly's captivity
- Why closure is a myth and how survival stories become cages
